findings.title: User OAuth token for each individual account
findings.detail: The list_folder endpoint accepts an OAuth 2.0 token issued to a specific user, and apps requesting only User API scopes receive a token associated with the authorizing user.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects an individual Dropbox account and no team administration is used.

evidence.quote: - `Authorization` header (bearer token, required) — OAuth 2.0 token issued to a specific user. Use `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Public clients should use the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256).
Apps that request only scopes from the User API will receive a token associated with the user that authorizes the app.
Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0, an open specification, to authorize access to a user’s data. Once completed by a user, the OAuth flow returns an access token to your app. This

findings.title: files.metadata.read for listing folder entries
findings.detail: files.metadata.read is the required scope for list_folder and list_folder/continue. Within the App Folder setting, it allows listing metadata only in the app folder.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing file and folder names in the App Folder, including continuation pages.

evidence.quote: **Required scope:** `files.metadata.read` **Endpoint format:** RPC
list_folder. **Required scope:** `files.metadata.read`
* **App Folder:** Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder *only* (in the /apps folder). This option is suitable

findings.title: Register the app with App Folder access and redirect URIs
findings.detail: The app must be registered in the Developer Console to obtain the app key and secret, configure redirect URIs, and select App Folder content access. Customers then connect through the OAuth flow rather than registering their own app.
findings.appliesWhen: Before the first test of the customer authorization flow.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you'll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the Developer Console. That page will guide you through the process
* You'll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console for your application. Add them under **Redirect URIs** in the OAuth 2 section
* **App Folder:** Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder *only* (in the /apps folder). This option is suitable

findings.title: Request only the minimal scope for app review
findings.detail: Dropbox advises requesting the least amount of permissions required, since broader requests may reduce acceptance and can affect app review.
findings.appliesWhen: Before submitting the app for launch with the files.metadata.read scope.

evidence.quote: ### Minimal Access Always ask for the *least* amount permissions required by your applications. Requesting more scope and content access than required may result in end users not accepting your
OAuth request and could impact your app review process.

steps.title: Register the Dropbox app with App Folder access and redirect URI
steps.detail: Create the app in the Dropbox Developer Console, choose the App Folder content access, enable the files.metadata.read scope, and register the exact redirect URI. Keep the app key (client_id) and app secret (client_secret) for the code exchange. Customers connect through OAuth; they do not register their own app.
steps.doneWhen: The app shows App Folder access, files.metadata.read is selected, the redirect URI is registered, and the app key and secret are stored securely.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you'll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the Developer Console. That page will guide you through the process
of registering your app, selecting permissions, and obtaining an app key and secret (a.k.a. `client_id` and `client_secret`) and inputting redirect URIs.
* You'll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console for your application. Add them under **Redirect URIs** in the OAuth 2 section

fields: Exact redirect URI registered under Redirect URIs

steps.title: Open the consent URL and capture the authorization code
steps.detail: Open the documented authorization URL in a browser for the individual customer account. The customer signs in on dropbox.com and approves the app. Dropbox redirects to the registered redirect URI with a code query parameter. Include token_access_type=offline only if a refresh token is needed.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect contains a code query parameter for the same app key and redirect URI; the consent is for the individual account, not a team.

evidence.quote: 1. Construct a Dropbox authorization URL, with your application’s `client_id` and `redirect_uri` (if applicable) and specifying the `response_type` of `code`, and present it to the user

`https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=MY_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=MY_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code` 2. Wait for the end user to complete authorization on dropbox.com, whom is then redirected back to your URI with an authorization code
of the Settings tab. Dropbox checks that the specified `redirect_uri` parameter in your Authorization URL matches one of the registered values at authorization time.

fields: APP_KEY: app key from the Developer Console
REDIRECT_URI: must exactly match a registered redirect URI
Authorization code is read from the callback query string

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Call the token endpoint with the authorization code, grant_type=authorization_code, redirect_uri, and the app secret using HTTP basic authentication. The response contains the short-lived access_token used as a Bearer token. Keep it out of logs.
steps.doneWhen: The response includes access_token and an expiry; the token is stored securely and not printed.

evidence.quote: 3. Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s `client_secret` to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls

When using refresh tokens, your call to the /oauth2/token endpoint with the `grant_type` of `authorization_code` will return a short-lived access token and a refresh token, which should be securely stored.

fields: AUTHORIZATION_CODE: code from the callback query string, used once
APP_KEY and APP_SECRET from the Developer Console
REDIRECT_URI must match the authorization request

steps.title: List the App Folder root (first page)
steps.detail: Call list_folder with path set to an empty string to request App Folder root entries, non-recursively. Record entries, cursor and has_more. Boundary check: confirm the grant is files.metadata.read only and the request log contains only list_folder calls with no download, upload, move or delete requests.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns entries and a cursor; has_more is recorded to decide continuation. Boundary check: confirm only files.metadata.read is granted and no content or write requests were sent.

evidence.quote: # List Folder POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/files/list_folder
Successful response - `cursor` (string, required) — Pass the cursor into list_folder/continue to see what's changed in the folder since your previous query.
- `entries` (list of files.Metadata, required) — The files and (direct) subfolders in the folder.

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN from the code exchange response
path empty string means the App Folder root

steps.title: Continue the App Folder listing until has_more is false
steps.detail: While has_more is true, call list_folder/continue with the cursor from the previous list_folder or list_folder/continue response and append each page's entries. Stop only when has_more is false. Boundary check: confirm only files.metadata.read is used and no content or write requests were sent.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are fetched by repeating list_folder/continue with the newest cursor until has_more is false; every page's entries are collected. Boundary check: confirm only files.metadata.read is used and no content or write requests were sent.

evidence.quote: Once a cursor has been retrieved from list_folder, use this to paginate through all
- `cursor` (string, required) — The cursor returned by your last call to list_folder or list_folder/continue.
- `has_more` (boolean, required) — If true, then there are more entries available. Pass the cursor to list_folder/continue to retrieve the rest.

fields: CURSOR_FROM_PRIOR_RESPONSE: cursor from the previous list_folder or list_folder/continue response
Repeat while has_more is true; stop when false
ACCESS_TOKEN from the code exchange response

steps.title: List the first page of a nested App Folder subfolder
steps.detail: For each folder entry whose contents must be listed, call list_folder with that folder's path_display (from the root listing) to get its direct children. Keep the child folder IDs and paths for recursive continuation. Boundary check: confirm only files.metadata.read is used and the request log holds no download or write calls.
steps.doneWhen: The subfolder returns its first entries, cursor and has_more; child folder paths are retained for their own continuation. Boundary check: confirm only files.metadata.read is used and no content or write requests were sent.

evidence.quote: # List Folder POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/files/list_folder
Successful response - `cursor` (string, required) — Pass the cursor into list_folder/continue to see what's changed in the folder since your previous query.
- `has_more` (boolean, required) — If true, then there are more entries available. Pass the cursor to list_folder/continue to retrieve the rest.

fields: SUBFOLDER_PATH: path_display of a folder entry from the App Folder listing
ACCESS_TOKEN from the code exchange response
